question.text: The distinction between speculative and hedging transactions in commodity derivatives affects:

answer.text: Tax treatment — hedging income is business income while speculative income has set-off restrictions
Exchange fees — hedgers pay lower fees
Margin requirements — speculators need no margin

explanation.text: The Logic: The principal practical difference between hedging and speculative commodity derivative transactions lies in tax treatment. A bona fide hedge (linked to a physical exposure) generally produces normal business income, which can be set off freely. A speculative transaction produces speculative business income, whose losses are ring-fenced and can only be set off against speculative profits. The Trap: Exchange fees and margin requirements are largely uniform across participant categories — they are not the basis for distinguishing hedgers from speculators. The hedge-vs-speculation distinction is highly meaningful precisely because of the tax consequence, not because of fees or margin. Note: The Series XVI Commodity Derivatives workbook pages reviewed distinguish hedging from speculative transactions but do not state that the distinction drives business-income versus speculative-income tax treatment with set-off restrictions. The framing above reflects general Indian income-tax practice rather than a workbook citation.
